Plus AI agents, NFL Week 2, MLB, UFC and The Trenches. GM. Get Money. 1% Better Every Day.

newsStories.headline: THE BIG STORY · SEC OPENS THE DOOR TO TOKENIZED STOCKS
newsStories.dek: A five-year innovation exemption creates a U.S. pathway for tokenized NMS stocks and pushes markets closer to 24/7 onchain trading.
newsStories.body: The SEC issued temporary conditional relief for Tokenized Securities Venues. Reuters reports the exemption lasts five years and can allow tokenized U.S. stocks to trade on blockchain-based venues with 24/7 access, instant settlement, fractional ownership and self-custody. This is not a free-for-all: issuers must be notified and can object, synthetic stock exposure is excluded, and qualifying tokenized shares must preserve the shareholder rights and disclosures of the conventional security.
newsStories.takeaway: THIS IS A MUCH BIGGER STORY THAN ANOTHER TOKENIZED-STOCK LAUNCH. THE U.S. REGULATOR JUST CREATED AN ACTUAL LANE FOR THE MARKET TO DEVELOP.

newsStories.headline: FED HIKES · FIRST INCREASE SINCE 2023
newsStories.dek: The Fed raised its target range 25 basis points to 3.75%-4.00% as inflation remains elevated.
newsStories.body: The FOMC voted 12-0 Wednesday to raise the federal funds target range by a quarter point. The Fed said economic activity is expanding at a solid pace, employment remains steady and inflation is still elevated. Markets are now trying to determine whether this is a one-off adjustment or the beginning of a broader tightening cycle.
newsStories.takeaway: YESTERDAY WE WERE ASKING IF THE FED WOULD HIKE. TODAY WE KNOW. NOW THE TRADE IS ABOUT WHAT COMES NEXT.

newsStories.headline: BITCOIN · THE DOUBLE WHAMMY
newsStories.dek: The failed CLARITY vote and the Fed hike landed back-to-back while ETF money moved out.
newsStories.body: Today's alert describes Bitcoin being hit by the combination of the Senate's CLARITY Act rejection and the Fed's first hike in three years. U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded roughly $450 million in net outflows around the policy shock, with the digest citing $450.33 million for September 15, the largest daily withdrawal since June 25.
points: LIVE CHART · LET PRICE TELL US WHAT HAPPENS NEXT
newsStories.takeaway: BITCOIN DIDN'T GET ONE MACRO HEADWIND. IT GOT WASHINGTON AND THE FED BACK-TO-BACK.
newsStories.source: Bloomberg / Yahoo Finance / Investing.com via Sep 17 digest

newsStories.headline: CLARITY AFTERMATH · THE FIGHT MOVES TO REGULATORS
newsStories.dek: Congress stalled, but the SEC is already showing that regulation isn't standing still.
newsStories.body: The digest says the CLARITY Act failed 49-50 on a procedural vote requiring 60 votes, while industry participants and banking groups are already preparing for the next round. At the same time, the SEC's tokenized-stock exemption shows regulators can still reshape digital-asset markets even while comprehensive legislation remains unresolved.
newsStories.takeaway: CONGRESS HIT A WALL. THE REGULATORY STORY DIDN'T STOP — IT JUST MOVED TO A DIFFERENT BUILDING.
newsStories.source: Yahoo Finance / Politico / Reuters / SEC via Sep 17 digest

robinhoodStories.headline: ONCHAIN WALL STREET · CIRCLE ARC IS LIVE
robinhoodStories.dek: Circle launched Arc mainnet for payments, markets and agentic economic activity with major institutions securing the network.
robinhoodStories.body: Circle says Arc launched publicly with more than 100 institutional and ecosystem builders. The network is purpose-built for financial markets, real-time money movement and agentic economic activity, with a founding validator cohort drawn from global financial institutions. Today's alert highlights BlackRock, DTCC, ICE, Visa and Mastercard among the names involved.
points: BLACKROCK / DTCC / ICE / VISA / MASTERCARD · ALERT HIGHLIGHTS
robinhoodStories.takeaway: THIS IS THE VERSION OF BLOCKCHAIN ADOPTION THAT LOOKS LESS LIKE CRYPTO TWITTER AND MORE LIKE FINANCIAL INFRASTRUCTURE.
robinhoodStories.source: Circle / Yahoo Finance via Sep 17 digest

robinhoodStories.headline: S&P GLOBAL BUYS OPENZEPPELIN · THE SECURITY LAYER GETS INSTITUTIONAL
robinhoodStories.dek: S&P Global agreed to acquire one of the best-known names in smart-contract security.
robinhoodStories.body: S&P Global announced an agreement today to acquire OpenZeppelin. S&P says OpenZeppelin Contracts underpin more than $37 trillion in value transferred and the company has completed more than 900 security engagements. OpenZeppelin will continue operating under its own name as a business unit. Financial terms were not disclosed.
points: ONCHAIN RISK ASSESSMENT · MOVING INTO TRADFI
robinhoodStories.takeaway: WHEN S&P GLOBAL BUYS SMART-CONTRACT SECURITY INFRASTRUCTURE, 'WALL STREET IS MOVING ONCHAIN' STOPS SOUNDING LIKE A SLOGAN.

robinhoodStories.headline: DEUTSCHE BANK · CRYPTO CUSTODY FOR INSTITUTIONS
robinhoodStories.dek: Another major bank is building regulated infrastructure around BTC and ETH custody.
robinhoodStories.body: Today's alert highlights reports that Deutsche Bank is launching or planning institutional crypto custody services for Bitcoin and Ether. The useful angle isn't a one-day price reaction; it's the cumulative buildout of regulated custody, security and market infrastructure around digital assets.
points: ADOPTION · BUILT ONE PIPE AT A TIME
robinhoodStories.takeaway: THE INSTITUTIONAL STORY ISN'T ONE BIG BANG. IT'S BANK AFTER BANK ADDING THE PIPES.

aiStories.headline: AI AGENTS · YOUR SMART HOME IS BECOMING AN API
aiStories.dek: Google's new MCP integration can let third-party AI agents control Google Home devices and data.
aiStories.body: The Verge item in today's alert says Google's Model Context Protocol integration will let AI agents such as Claude and OpenClaw interact with Google Home devices and data. Nature also highlights Paper2Agent, a framework that can turn scientific papers into interactive AI agents. The common thread is agents moving from chat interfaces into real-world systems and specialized work.
points: AGENTS · MOVING FROM TALKING TO DOING
aiStories.takeaway: THE AGENT STORY IS GETTING REAL WHEN THE SOFTWARE STOPS ANSWERING QUESTIONS AND STARTS OPERATING THINGS.
aiStories.source: The Verge / Nature via Sep 17 digest
